target: leaf adaxial epidermis (PO_0006018)
reason: Narrower: 'epidermal layer' is an exact synonym of plant epidermis (PO_0005679), and 'adaxial' places it on the upper side of the leaf. The statements ('adaxial epidermal layer of cells not differentiated / absent') describe leaf (and moss phyllid) anatomy, and PO lists 'phyllid epidermis' under leaf epidermis. Other organs (sepal, petal, bract) have their own adaxial epidermis classes if the context names them.

target: count of septum (PO_0000030) by pattern 03: add a row 'septate -> septum' to config/flora_counted_parts.tsv
reason: '0-1-septate' is a compound count word like '5-nerved'. It gives the number of cross-walls in a hair, cell or spore. The part is the septum; the bearer comes from the noun it describes ('hyaline cells').

target: position of the bearer (pattern 04) on the noun it describes (branch, capsule)
reason: A position word ('intercalary branches', 'intercalary, sterile ...'): it means inserted between other parts of a series. It describes a state of the part, not a part.

target: fruit valve (PO_0000033)
reason: Narrower: a valve of a legume fruit (PO_0030100, synonym 'pod'). The fruit valve class covers it; the legume can be added as the qualified whole (pattern 12) if needed.

target: microsporophyll (PO_0009028)
reason: Narrower: the French statements ('écailles staminales spiralées, limbe triangulaire, irrégulièrement denticulé aux bords') describe spirally arranged scales with a stalk and a blade, bearing pollen sacs, in a male cone (cycads and other gymnosperms). That is a microsporophyll. If an angiosperm flora uses the word for a scale-like staminode, the bearer is staminode (PO_0009077), so check the family before applying the rule.

Raphides are needle-shaped calcium oxalate crystals inside cells: a substance in a cell, not a plant part. This follows the decision on 'crystal'. The cell that holds them is an idioblast (PO_0000283), if a bearer is wanted.

target: peduncle (PO_0009053) at fruit development stage (PO_0001002), via the context word 'fruiting'
reason: Narrower: the peduncle of an inflorescence that is in fruit. The stage is already handled by flora_context_words.tsv ('fruiting' -> PO_0001002), the same way as the fruiting calyx. This is not fruit pedicel (PO_0030114), which is the stalk of a single fruit.

target: vascular bundle (PO_0005020)
reason: Narrower: extra vascular bundles beside the main ones, given only as counts ('3-7 accessory bundles'). Use a count of vascular bundles (pattern 03) with the container named in the statement. 'Accessory' does not need its own class.
A size word ('4 tiny teeth', 'tiny leaflets'). The counted part is the noun after it (tubercle, tooth, leaflet).

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) as the distal region of sporophyll (PO_0009026), or megasporophyll (PO_0009027) when the cone is female
reason: The 'terminal facet' (hexagonal, rhomboid, concave, cushion-like) is the exposed outer face of a cone scale, as in Zamia and other cycads. It is the end region of the sporophyll, so the apex region pattern can express it without a new class.

target: anther wing (proposed new class, batch 0035): the pair of adjacent anther wings of the gynostegium (FLOPO_0986051)
reason: In Asclepiadoideae the guide rail is the slit formed by the wings of two neighbouring anthers. Its traits (straight, protruding, exposed, cream, length) are traits of those anther wings. The anther wing proposal already lists 'guide rail wing' as a synonym, so a separate class is not needed.

label: translator
parent: is_a PO_0009011 (plant structure); part_of pollinarium (proposed new class, batch 0036)
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) of an Apocynaceae flower that is secreted by the style head of the gynostegium (FLOPO:0986051) and attaches the pollen or pollinia (FLOPO:0986016) to a pollinator. It is spoon-shaped in Periplocoideae; in Secamonoideae and Asclepiadoideae it is made of a corpusculum and two translator arms. NOTE: Propose to PO with gynostegium, pollinarium and corpusculum (PO issue 6).
reason: A standard character in Apocynaceae that both floras describe (shape: triangular or elliptic; arm length). No PO or FLOPO class covers it. A translator arm is a part of it: either a part of the translator (pattern 12) or, if the curator prefers, the caudicle class (FLOPO_0986033). Corpusculum and pollinarium were already proposed, so this fills the gap between them.

target: count of rib (pattern 03) with container cypsela (FLOPO_0986053)
reason: Only counts ('ribs 15-20'). The 'rib' counted part already exists (ribbed/costate rows in flora_counted_parts.tsv), and cypsela has a class, so the pattern covers it.

target: spine leaf (PO_0025173) part of areole bud (PO_0025353), position in the series: central, inner
reason: Cactus areole spines. Earlier decisions handled central, peripheral and subcentral spines the same way: an areole spine plus a position. 'Inner central' is one more position in that series; counts are per areole.

target: inflorescence branch (PO_0009081)
reason: Narrower: the branches of a panicle-like inflorescence that are themselves racemes ('5-20 racemose branches'). PO's inflorescence branch is the bearer for the count. Their raceme form, if needed, is raceme inflorescence (PO_0030115).

target: ratio to another part (pattern 10) with the reference part sepal (PO_0009031)
reason: 'Petals 1.5-2 times as long as sepals' compares lengths. The bearer is the subject of the sentence (petal, pedicel). The sepal is the second part of the comparison, not a new part.

target: fruit distal end (PO_0008001) with a concave/depressed shape and depth
reason: The umbilicus ('3-4 mm deep', 'slightly depressed') is the hollow at the top of a fruit where the flower fell off, as in cacti. It is a region of the fruit tip, and its depth and depression are qualities of that region. This is not the seed hilum (PO_0020063).

target: count of the subject part per whorl (pattern 03); arrangement whorled (PATO_0001951)
reason: 'Flowers 10-20 in whorls' counts the subject (flowers, leaves) per whorl and says they are whorled. The whorl is the counting unit. If the whorl itself must be a bearer, it is collective phyllome structure (PO_0025023, synonym 'whorl').

target: short shoot (PO_0004701)
reason: Narrower: 'axillary leaf fascicles', 'sterile, small spiny leaf fascicles' are clusters of leaves on short shoots in the leaf axils (Lycium, Berberis and similar plants). PO's short shoot is the bearer. If only the leaves are meant, use collective leaf structure (PO_0025022) instead.

target: leaf stomatal complex (PO_0025183), in rows/lines per leaf surface (abaxial/adaxial position)
reason: Same as the earlier decision on 'stomatal row': lines of stomata on the leaf surfaces of conifers. Presence and number are said of the stomatal complexes, placed by surface.

target: staminal corona (FLOPO_0985022)
reason: Narrower/near-exact: in Apocynaceae the gynostegial corona grows from the stamens of the gynostegium ('Gynostegial corona of fused staminal ...'). So the staminal corona class fits. Corona lobes use corona lobe (FLOPO_0986035). Interstaminal parts can use floral corona (FLOPO_0985020) instead.

target: perigynium (PO_0009044)
reason: Exact, just cut short: the traits ('apical teeth', 'sharp edged to base', 'puncticulate', 'oblong-orbicular') are those of the Carex perigynium. Do not confuse it with the floral adjective 'perigynous'.
A word that ranks members of a set ('central 3 dominant'), not a part. The counted part is the noun before it (branches).

target: plant organ lamina (PO_0025513) part of orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978); outside Orchidaceae part of corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017)
reason: The flat expanded part of the lip, as opposed to its claw or base. It is a lamina of a qualified whole (pattern 12). Margin and apex traits ('margin crenulate', 'apex truncate') go to the margin and apex regions of the lip. The plant family decides which lip class applies.

target: shoot-borne root spine (PO_0030089)
reason: Exact in sense: rings of hardened, pointed roots at culm nodes (bamboos, some palms) are shoot-borne roots that became spines. That is PO's definition (sclerified, pointed). Lateral root spine (PO_0030088) applies only to spines on roots.

target: wrinkled (PATO_0001810) on the noun described; the number of transverse wrinkles as a count (pattern 03) only if the curator wants it
reason: A wrinkle is a fold in a surface, not an anatomical part. The surface's quality is wrinkled or rugose, and the count is an extra detail of that quality.

target: anastomosing (FLOPO:0991128) on leaf lamina vein (PO_0020138); the number of anastomoses as a count on the veins
reason: 'Vein anastomoses 1-3' counts the points where veins join. A joining point is a relation between veins, not a part. The value class for anastomosing veins already exists.

target: cardinal organ part (PO_0025001) part of gynostemium (FLOPO_0986015), with the 'tooth' counted part (pattern 03 / 12)
reason: In orchids the column is the gynostemium, and its teeth (stelidia) are small outgrowths at its tip. They are teeth of a named whole, so the 'tooth' counted part and the part-of-a-whole pattern cover them. A stelidium class could come later if more floras need it.

target: stalk (PO_0025066) part of pinna (FLOPO_0985027), pattern 12
reason: The stalk of a fern or palm pinna. PO's petiolule is the stalk of a leaflet, and FLOPO keeps pinna separate from leaflet, so stalk as part of a pinna is the correct form. It needs no new class.

target: stalk (PO_0025066) part of pinnule (FLOPO_0985028), pattern 12
reason: Same as pinna stalk, one division further down: the short stalk of a pinnule (winged, terete, length).
